samples.question: The picture is one square quilt of 6 rows by 6 columns of touching tiles. Columns 1-3 are the LEFT block and columns 4-6 are the RIGHT block. Every tile has one fill colour (red, blue, green or purple) and one white mark. The right block's marks were copied from the left block by rotating that block 180 degrees: the mark of the right-block tile in row r of right-block column c should equal the mark of the left-block tile in row 7-r, left-block column 4-c. The marks themselves were copied without being rotated. Exactly two right-block tiles break this rule, because their two marks were exchanged with each other; every other right-block tile matches its rotated partner exactly. Fill colours follow no rule and say nothing about which tiles those are. Of the two exchanged tiles, take the one that comes first in reading order: the smaller row number, or if the rows are equal the smaller column number. What is the fill colour of that tile? Answer red, blue, green or purple.
